digest.top_line: Adjuvant pelvic IMRT post-cystectomy: 2y LRFS 87.1% v 76.0%, HR 0.43 (0.20-0.96), P=.04, the first positive randomised adjuvant RT signal in MIBC.
digest.tldr: A day about what nodal RT buys and for how long. Bladder gets the first randomised win for adjuvant pelvic IMRT, but only on the locoregional endpoint (DFS/BCSS/OS CIs all cross 1). Breast cuts the other way: EORTC 22922 at 20yr shows IM-MS-RT's 3.8-pt BC-mortality gain erased by excess non-BC deaths (OS HR 1.00), and RxPONDER's RNI analysis finds LRR <1% either way in RS≤25 N1 disease.

sites.intro: First randomised evidence that adjuvant pelvic RT improves locoregional control after radical cystectomy, in a control arm that predates adjuvant nivolumab.

studies.name: Bladder Adjuvant Radiotherapy Trial
studies.tldr: 2y LRFS 87.1% v 76.0%, HR 0.43 (0.20-0.96), P=.04 for adjuvant pelvic IMRT post-cystectomy in high-risk MIBC.
details: 🔍 Phase III multicenter RCT, N=153 (RT 77, Obs 76), accrual Jun 2016 to May 2024, median f/u 47mo
🔍 High-risk eligibility: any of T3-4, N1-3, margin positive, or ≤10 nodes dissected
📐 Stratified by nodal involvement (yes/no) and chemo timing (neoadj/adj/none)
📊 Baseline risk: 62% pT3-T4, 41% pN+; >90% received systemic chemo (71% neoadjuvant, 20% adjuvant)

details.text: 📊 RT vs Obs across endpoints (2y rates, HR)

details: ⚠️ Only the 1° locoregional endpoint crosses significance; DFS, BCSS and OS CIs all cross 1
⚠️ N=153 over 8 years of accrual; underpowered for survival endpoints, and the LRFS CI upper bound is 0.96
⚠️ No pt received immunotherapy, so the control arm predates adjuvant nivolumab (CheckMate 274) as post-RC standard
🔗 First positive randomised adjuvant RT signal in MIBC; prior evidence was the underaccrued Egyptian NCI trial and retrospective series

verdict.rationale: Randomised, prespecified 1° endpoint met, but N=153 and locoregional-only benefit; control arm has no adjuvant IO, so it contests observation rather than establishing RT.
verdict.audience: Post-cystectomy MIBC: pT3-4, N+, margin+, or ≤10 nodes dissected

studies.significance: The transferable detail is technique: stoma-sparing IG-IMRT, 50.4Gy/28fx to cystectomy bed plus pelvic nodes, with no additional severe toxicity reported. That is a deliverable prescription for a field most rad oncs have avoided post-RC, and it moves the offer-vs-observe decision in pN+ or margin-positive pts, where 41% of this cohort sat.
studies.monday_clinic: In post-cystectomy MIBC with pT3-4, pN+, positive margins, or ≤10 nodes dissected who have had perioperative chemotherapy, this supports discussing adjuvant pelvic RT rather than observation alone; it does not speak to pts receiving adjuvant immunotherapy, since none were enrolled.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Phase III multicenter randomized trial, **1:1 adjuvant RT versus observation**, stratified by nodal involvement and chemotherapy timing. **153 pts** randomized Jun 2016 to May 2024, median follow-up **47 months**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Nonmetastatic urothelial MIBC at high risk after radical cystectomy: **any one of T3-4, N1-3, margin positive, or ≤10 nodes dissected**. **62% pT3-T4**, **41% pN+**. Over 90% received systemic chemotherapy (71% neoadjuvant, 20% adjuvant); **none received immunotherapy**.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **Stoma-sparing IG-IMRT, 50.4Gy in 28 fractions**, prescribed to the **cystectomy bed and pelvic nodes**. The conclusion reports **no additional severe toxicity** versus observation.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: 2-year locoregional recurrence-free survival.** Secondary: disease-free survival, bladder cancer-specific survival, overall survival.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: The primary locoregional endpoint was met; **all three survival secondaries favored RT numerically with CIs crossing 1**. Per-endpoint rates and hazard ratios are in the comparison table.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents chemotherapy-treated, high-risk post-cystectomy urothelial MIBC with pT3-4, pN+, positive margins, or limited nodal dissection. Does not represent pts receiving adjuvant immunotherapy, node-negative organ-confined disease, or nonurothelial histology.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The **8-year accrual window** spans a period in which post-cystectomy systemic therapy changed, and zero immunotherapy use makes the observation arm a **historical control** by 2026 practice. Toxicity is asserted in the conclusion without grade-level numbers in the source abstract, so the therapeutic-ratio claim cannot be audited here.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Technique is the transferable part: stoma-sparing IG-IMRT, 50.4Gy/28fx to the cystectomy bed and pelvic nodes, no additional severe toxicity reported. That is a deliverable prescription for a post-RC field most rad oncs have avoided, and it moves the offer-vs-observe decision in pN+ or margin-positive pts.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Over 90% had perioperative chemotherapy (71% neoadjuvant) and **none** had immunotherapy, so this tests RT on a chemo backbone, not against adjuvant nivolumab. The locoregional gain does not resolve how RT sequences with or substitutes for adjuvant IO in the same high-risk group.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Two of the four entry criteria are surgical quality markers: positive margins and ≤10 nodes dissected. The locoregional benefit concentrates where the operation left residual risk, so pathology reporting of margin status and node yield is what triages a pt toward this discussion.

open_questions: Does adjuvant RT add to adjuvant immunotherapy post-cystectomy?
Which high-risk subgroup drives the locoregional benefit?
Does locoregional control translate to overall survival with longer follow-up?

sites.intro: Two reads on nodal irradiation: 20yr competing mortality in EORTC 22922, and a genomically-selected N1 population where the LRR floor leaves RNI almost nothing to prevent.

studies.name: SWOG S1007
studies.tldr: 5yr LRR 0.85% with RNI vs 0.55% without after BCS+RT in RS≤25 N1 disease; IDFS unchanged by RNI.
details: 🔍 Secondary analysis of RxPONDER (S1007): HR+/ERBB2- , 1-3 nodes, Oncotype RS ≤25, randomized to ET vs chemo→ET
📊 RNI practice was split: 2274/3852 (59.0%) of irradiated pts with complete target data received RNI
📊 3947/4871 (81.0%) with RT forms reported RT receipt; median f/u 6.1 yrs
📐 IDFS by RNI receipt, premenopausal HR 1.03 (0.74-1.43), P=.87; postmenopausal HR 0.85 (0.68-1.07), P=.16

details.text: 📊 5yr cumulative incidence of LRR by locoregional treatment

details: 📊 LRR similarly low in the chemo-omission (ET-alone) group, so dropping chemo did not raise the RNI bar
🔍 RNI defined as targeting at least the supraclavicular region; RT data collected in yr 1, so survival analyses landmarked at 1 yr
⚠️ Non-randomized RT comparison: RNI receipt was physician-choice, so confounding by indication cuts both ways despite adjustment
⚠️ Event counts are tiny (LRR <1% in most strata), so this bounds the absolute benefit rather than excluding a relative one
🔗 Contrast with MA.20 / EORTC 22922, where RNI improved DFS/distant control in a mostly higher-risk, pre-genomic N1 population

verdict.rationale: Secondary, non-randomized analysis of RT receipt within an RCT; RNI not allocated. Low absolute LRR supports, not proves, safe omission in favorable N1.
verdict.audience: HR+/ERBB2- breast, 1-3 positive nodes, Oncotype RS ≤25

studies.significance: The number that moves the nodal decision is 0.55% 5yr LRR after BCS + breast RT alone, and 1.7% after mastectomy with no RT at all, in RS ≤25 N1 disease. Chemo omission did not raise LRR, so it is not an independent trigger for supraclavicular coverage.
studies.monday_clinic: In HR+/ERBB2- breast cancer with 1-3 nodes and Oncotype RS ≤25 treated with BCS, this supports discussing RNI omission on absolute-risk grounds; it does not extend to RS >25, higher nodal burden, or ERBB2+/triple-negative disease.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Secondary analysis of the **SWOG S1007 (RxPONDER)** randomized trial, using **prospectively collected** radiotherapy forms from **4871** patients treated in diverse settings. Data analyzed June 2022 to April 2023, median follow-up **6.1 years**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Hormone receptor-positive, **ERBB2-negative** breast cancer with **1 to 3 involved nodes** and an Oncotype DX 21-gene **Recurrence Score ≤25**. Median age **57** (range 18-87), all female.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **RNI defined as targeting at least the supraclavicular region.** Of 3852 irradiated patients with complete target information, **2274 (59.0%)** received RNI, so practice was close to evenly split. Dose and fractionation not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Cumulative incidence of LRR** by locoregional treatment received, plus the association between **IDFS** and locoregional therapy, adjusted for menopausal status, treatment group, recurrence score, tumor size, nodes involved and axillary surgery. Survival analyses **landmarked at 1 year** because RT data were captured in the first year.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: IDFS did not differ by RNI receipt in either menopausal stratum (**HR 1.03**, 0.74-1.43 premenopausal; **HR 0.85**, 0.68-1.07 postmenopausal). LRR was low across every locoregional strategy, including in patients assigned endocrine therapy alone.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: MA.20 and EORTC 22922 established RNI benefit in a **higher-risk, pre-genomic** N1 population with older systemic therapy. This cohort is selected for **favorable biology (RS ≤25)** and modern axillary management, which is where the absolute LRR floor collapses.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents HR+/ERBB2- N1 breast cancer with Oncotype RS ≤25 and modern surgical and systemic therapy. Does not represent RS >25, ERBB2+ or triple-negative disease, ≥4 positive nodes, or patients staged outside a cooperative-group trial.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: RT target data were captured only in the first post-randomization year, so late or salvage RT is invisible and the landmark excludes early events. **1019 of 4871** patients lacked complete target information, and RNI assignment was clinician-driven rather than randomized.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The authors' framing is the practical one: **omission of chemotherapy is not an independent indication for RNI**. With LRR under 1% after breast-conserving surgery and RT without RNI, the nodal decision in this biology rests on competing risk of toxicity, not on a measurable local-control gap.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: 0.55% 5yr LRR after BCS + breast RT without RNI, versus 0.85% with it, sets the absolute ceiling on what supraclavicular coverage can buy in RS ≤25 N1 disease. RNI was defined as at least supraclavicular targeting, so the omission question here is nodal fields, not breast RT itself.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Chemo omission in RS ≤25 N1 disease did not produce a higher LRR signal, and IDFS was unchanged by RNI receipt in both menopausal strata. De-escalating systemic therapy therefore does not obligate a compensatory escalation of nodal radiotherapy.

open_questions: Does RNI omission hold beyond 5 years in RS 21-25 N1 disease
Optimal nodal target volume when axillary dissection is omitted

studies.name: EORTC 22922/10925
studies.tldr: 20yr OS 61.8% vs 61.0% (HR 1.00, p=.967) with IM-MS nodal RT; breast cancer mortality fell, non-BC deaths rose.
details: 🔍 Phase 3 multicentre RCT, N=4004 randomized 1996-2004, median age 54, median f/u 22.2 yrs
🔍 Eligible: stage I-III, involved axillary nodes and/or central/medial tumor regardless of nodal status
📊 1550 (38.7%) deaths total; 796 (51.4%) of those from breast cancer

details.text: 📊 Any breast cancer recurrence: HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.78-0.99), p=.0369, from the figure panel
⚠️ Late toxicity higher with IM-MS-RT (IM-MS-RT vs no IM-MS-RT)

details: ⚠️ Non-BC deaths diverged after 15 yrs, cancelling the 3.8-point absolute BC-mortality gain
⚠️ RT delivered 1996-2004: 2D/3D era heart and lung dose, not deep-inspiration breath-hold or IMRT

details.text: 🔗 Contrast with the trial's own 10yr read, where the OS curve had not yet been overtaken by competing mortality

verdict.rationale: Prespecified 20yr analysis of a 4004-pt randomised trial, primary endpoint null; the disease benefit is real but offset by excess non-BC death. Design internally valid.
verdict.audience: Stage I-III breast, node-positive and/or central/medial tumor, post-ALND

studies.significance: The trade is quantified: a 3.8-point absolute drop in breast cancer mortality (22.4% to 18.6%, HR 0.82) bought at a 4.6-point rise in non-BC death (15.8% to 20.4%, HR 1.26), with cardiac disease 15.2% vs 11.7% and lung fibrosis 6.3% vs 3.2%. The offset only appeared after 15 yrs, so this argues the IM-MS decision now turns on heart and lung dose, not on target selection.
studies.monday_clinic: In a node-positive or central/medial stage I-III breast pt with a long life expectancy, this supports treating IM-MS coverage as a cardiac and lung dose problem rather than a settled indication; it does not speak to pts planned with modern breath-hold or IMRT, whose competing-risk arm is untested.

primary_endpoint.name: Overall survival
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: HR 1.00, p=.967; primary endpoint not met

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Prospective multicenter randomized **phase 3** trial, accrual 1996-2004, **N=4004**. Planned from the outset for a final analysis at **20 years**, on the assumption that any survival effect of IM-MS-RT would not emerge before 10 years. Median follow-up **22.2 years**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Women **aged 75 or younger**, unilateral histologically confirmed breast adenocarcinoma, **stage I-III**. Eligible with a **centrally or medially located** primary irrespective of axillary involvement, or a primary in any quadrant with **axillary node involvement**. Median age 54.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Randomization was to **internal mammary and medial supraclavicular (levels 3-4) nodal irradiation** or no IM-MS-RT, layered on standard breast or chest wall treatment, with a **trial-integrated RT quality-assurance program**. Dose and fractionation are not given in the source excerpt.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: overall survival.** Secondary: disease-free survival, distant metastases-free survival, breast cancer mortality, and any breast recurrence.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: The primary endpoint was **not met**. The disease-directed endpoints split from the competing-risk endpoints, which is the whole finding: **no benefit** on OS, DFS or DMFS despite lower breast cancer mortality.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Lung fibrosis **6.3% vs 3.2%**, cardiac fibrosis **2.7% vs 1.7%**, cardiac disease **15.2% vs 11.7%** with IM-MS-RT. Severe (score 3-4) events were uncommon and close between arms: cardiac 1.9% vs 1.7%, lung 0.3% vs 0.0%.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents stage I-III breast cancer with involved axillary nodes and/or a central or medial primary, treated with surgery plus ALND in the 1996-2004 era. Does not represent pts planned with contemporary heart-sparing technique, nor those staged and treated by sentinel node biopsy alone.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Surgery, systemic therapy and RT planning all predate current practice, so the toxicity arm of the trade-off is likely overstated for a pt treated today while the disease benefit is likely understated. **Cause-of-death attribution** carries weight here: the non-BC and unknown-cause deaths are pooled into one 20.4% vs 15.8% comparison.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: A trial that was positive on breast cancer mortality and null on survival is the clearest available argument for very long follow-up in a good-prognosis disease: the competing-risk crossover only appeared **after 15 years**. The authors make that call explicitly.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The IM-MS target itself works: breast cancer mortality 22.4% to 18.6% (HR 0.82) and any breast recurrence HR 0.88 (0.78-0.99). What cancels it is dose to heart and lung, cardiac disease 15.2% vs 11.7% and lung fibrosis 6.3% vs 3.2% in 2D/3D-era plans. The decision moves from whether to cover IM-MS to how much OAR dose the plan can hold.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Competing mortality, not disease, drove the null: non-BC and unknown-cause deaths 20.4% vs 15.8% (HR 1.26), diverging only after 15 yrs. In a good-prognosis pt with decades of expected survival, this argues for weighting cardiovascular risk alongside recurrence risk when the regional nodal plan is being set.

open_questions: Does modern heart-sparing RT preserve the BC-mortality gain without the excess?
Which subgroups have enough recurrence risk to outweigh competing mortality?

papers.title: Twenty‐year results of the randomized European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer trial 22922/10925 evaluating internal mammary chain and medial supraclavicular lymph node irradiation in stage I–III breast cancer
authors: van den Bongard, Desirée H. J. G.
for the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Radiation Oncology and Breast Cancer Groups
papers.journal: CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians
papers.abstract: Abstract European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer trial EORTC 22922/10925 evaluated internal mammary and medial supraclavicular (IM‐MS) lymph node irradiation (IM‐MS‐RT) in patients with stage I–III breast cancer. Eligible patients had involved axillary nodes and/or centrally/medially located tumors regardless of nodal involvement. The primary end point was overall survival, secondary end points were disease‐free survival, distant metastases‐free survival, breast cancer mortality, and any breast recurrence. Between 1996 and 2004, 4004 patients were randomized. The median patient age was 54 years. At a median follow‐up of 22.2 years, 1550 (38.7%) patients died, of whom 796 (51.4%) died from breast cancer. At 20 years, the overall survival rate was 61.8% in the control group versus 61.0% in the IM‐MS‐RT group (hazard ratio [HR], 1.00; p = .967); the disease‐free survival rate was 49.0% versus 48.2%, respectively (HR, 0.97; p = .515); and the distant metastases‐free survival rate was 59.8% versus 58.9%, respectively (HR, 0.97; p = .578). The breast cancer mortality rate was 22.4% in the control group and 18.6% in the IM‐MS‐RT group (HR, 0.82; p = .006), whereas the rate of deaths not from breast cancer or from unknown causes was 15.8% versus 20.4%, respectively (HR, 1.26; p = .002). Lung fibrosis, cardiac fibrosis, and cardiac diseases were more frequent after IM‐MS‐RT versus no IM‐MS‐RT (6.3% vs. 3.2%, 2.7% vs. 1.7%. and 15.2% vs. 11.7%, respectively); and the rates of severe cardiac and lung morbidities (scores of 3 or 4) were 1.9% versus 1.7% and 0.3% versus 0.0%, respectively. Breast cancer mortality at 20 years was statistically significantly lower after IM‐MS‐RT, but deaths not from breast cancer increased after 15 years, resulting in no long‐term benefit of IM‐MS‐RT on overall survival. Therefore, the authors strongly call for very long‐term follow‐up of treatments for prognostically favorable cancers such as breast cancer.

papers.title: Bladder Adjuvant Radiotherapy: Phase III Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial of Adjuvant Radiotherapy or Observation for Postcystectomy Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: To report the primary analysis of a multicenter, phase III randomized trial of adjuvant radiotherapy (RT) after chemotherapy and radical cystectomy (RC) in patients with high-risk muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC).

METHODS: Patients with nonmetastatic urothelial MIBC at high risk after RC (any one of: T3-4, N1-3, margin positive, ≤10 nodes dissected) were randomly assigned 1:1 to adjuvant RT or observation (Obs), stratified by nodal involvement (yes/no) and chemotherapy (neoadjuvant/adjuvant/none). Stoma-sparing IG-IMRT 50.4Gy in 28 fractions was prescribed to the cystectomy bed and pelvic nodes. The primary end point was 2-year locoregional recurrence-free survival (LRFS), and the secondary end points were disease-free survival (DFS), bladder cancer-specific survival (BCSS), and overall survival (OS).

RESULTS: From June 2016 to May 2024, 153 patients were randomly assigned (Obs = 76, RT = 77), with 62% and 41% of patients having pT3-T4 and pN+ stages, respectively. Over 90% of the patients received systemic chemotherapy (71% neoadjuvant and 20% adjuvant), and none received immunotherapy. After a median follow-up of 47 months, the 2-year LRFS was significantly higher with adjuvant RT versus observation (87.1% v 76.0%, hazard ratio [HR], 0.43 [95% CI, 0.20 to 0.96], P = .04). The DFS was 71.6% versus 58.7% (HR, 0.62 [95% CI, 0.36 to 1.05]), BCSS was 79.6% versus 65.0% (HR, 0.59 [95% CI, 0.33 to 1.10]), and OS was 70.4% versus 57.4% (HR, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.49 to 1.26]) for RT and Obs, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Adjuvant pelvic IMRT after radical cystectomy and perioperative chemotherapy suggests an improvement in locoregional control in patients with high risk urothelial MIBC with no additional severe toxicity.

papers.title: Radiotherapy Use and Incidence of Locoregional Recurrence in Patients With Favorable-Risk, Node-Positive Breast Cancer Enrolled in the SWOG S1007 Trial.
papers.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Little is known about regional nodal irradiation (RNI) practice patterns or rates of locoregional recurrence (LRR) with and without RNI in patients with limited nodal disease and favorable biology treated with modern surgical and systemic therapy, including approaches that de-escalate those latter treatments.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate how often patients with low-recurrence score breast cancer with 1 to 3 nodes involved receive RNI, incidence and predictors of LRR, and associations between locoregional therapy and disease-free survival.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this secondary analysis of the SWOG S1007 trial, patients with hormone receptor-positive, ERBB2-negative breast cancer, and a Oncotype DX 21-gene Breast Recurrence Score assay result of no more than 25, were randomized to endocrine therapy alone vs chemotherapy then endocrine therapy. Prospectively collected radiotherapy information was collected from 4871 patients treated in diverse settings. Data were analyzed June 2022 to April 2023.

EXPOSURE: Receipt of RNI (targeting at least the supraclavicular region).

MAIN OUTCOME(S) AND MEASURE(S): Cumulative incidence of LRR was calculated by locoregional treatment received. Analyses were assessed for associations between invasive disease-free survival (IDFS) and locoregional therapy, adjusted for menopausal status, treatment group, recurrence score, tumor size, nodes involved, and axillary surgery. Radiotherapy information was recorded in the first year after randomization, so survival analyses were landmarked as starting at 1 year among those still at risk.

RESULTS: Of 4871 female patients (median [range] age, 57 [18-87] years) with radiotherapy forms, 3947 (81.0%) reported radiotherapy receipt. Of 3852 patients who received radiotherapy and had complete information on targets, 2274 (59.0%) received RNI. With a median follow-up of 6.1 years, the cumulative incidence of LRR by 5 years was 0.85% among patients who received breast-conserving surgery and radiotherapy with RNI; 0.55% after breast-conserving surgery with radiotherapy without RNI; 0.11% after mastectomy with postmastectomy radiotherapy; and 1.7% after mastectomy without radiotherapy. Similarly low LRR was observed within the group assigned to endocrine therapy without chemotherapy. The rate of IDFS did not differ by RNI receipt (premenopausal: hazard ratio [HR], 1.03; 95% CI, 0.74-1.43; P = .87; postmenopausal: HR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.68-1.07; P = .16).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this secondary analysis of a clinical trial, RNI use was divided in the setting of biologically favorable N1 disease, and rates of LRR were low even in patients who did not receive RNI. Disease-free survival was not associated with RNI receipt; omission of chemotherapy among patients similar to those enrolled in the S1007 trial is not an independent indication for use of RNI.
